question: A news site gave randomly chosen new comments one fake up-vote. How did those comments end up rated?
answer: About 25% higher than others. Muchnik, Aral and Taylor ran the test on a live site with over 100,000 comments: one early up-vote made the next reader about a third more likely to up-vote too, and the lead lasted. A random early down-vote, by contrast, was soon corrected by readers.
move: An early nudge can decide what looks like a crowd's free verdict.
ask: When I liked something because many others had, did I judge it for myself first?
trap: Readers judge each comment on its merits, so one vote washes out.
